claims.text: Machine-learning models using Hölder means of elemental properties and structural properties can be applied to multicomponent high-entropy materials.
The proposed machine-learning intervention will improve transition-temperature determination relative to experimental, DFT, and CALPHAD baselines.
The proposed machine-learning intervention will improve determination of fusion enthalpy and entropy.
The proposed machine-learning intervention will improve determination of the volume change at the solid-to-fluid transition.
The proposed machine-learning intervention will improve determination of dense-fluid heat capacity.
Machine learning will enable efficient screening of high-entropy-material compositions.
The target initial material is a multicomponent high-entropy alloy in its solid state.
The proposed intervention is incorporation of machine-learning models for prediction and screening.
The intervention is intended to operate at high temperatures and across various compositions.
Configurational entropy mediates the effect of the machine-learning intervention on the target transition properties.
Lattice distortion mediates the effect of the machine-learning intervention on the target transition properties.
Machine-learning models can learn property-relevant patterns from elemental and structural descriptors.
Patterns learned from elemental and structural descriptors are sufficient to predict high-temperature solid-to-fluid thermodynamic properties.
The resulting predictions can guide identification of optimal compositions and conditions for desired phase transitions.
The applicability of a machine-learning model is limited to systems and conditions represented by, or validated against, its training domain.
Generalization to unseen compositions and conditions is uncertain.
Overfitting or underfitting could limit the proposed model.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing predictions with experimental measurements for a set of high-entropy alloys.
Failure beyond a predefined error threshold for a substantial number of compositions would falsify the hypothesis.
